pr_title: Move cloud provider controllers to k8s.io/cloud-provider
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
We're trying to make `cmd/cloud-controller-manager` easier to consume (https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider/issues/29). This PR moves all the cloud provider specific controllers to k8s.io/cloud-provider as part of moving all of `cmd/cloud-controller-manager` eventually.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/81172

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

Moving the controller loops seems reasonable. Moving the v1alpha1 config struct which is tightly tied to the kube-controller-manager v1alpha1 config is less clear to me. Nothing inside the controller code references that config, there's a single option for the number of sync workers that is passed to the controller's constructor.

Additionally, it doesn't look like all the config type linting got wired up correctly to the new location. Can we limit this PR to moving the controller loops?

> Additionally, it doesn't look like all the config type linting got wired up correctly to the new location. Can we limit this PR to moving the controller loops?

sgtm, I'll update shortly

@liggitt moved versioned service controller config back to kube-controller-manager.

/retest
Should `cmd/cloud-controller-manager/.import-restrictions` also be modified due to cloud provider controller movement?

Chatted with Dims and Andrew. We agree that having KCM depend on the staging/cloud-provider repo for config is not ideal.  There is an upcoming PR moving GenericControllerManagerConfiguration , KubeCloudSharedConfiguration , ServiceControllerConfiguration , etc to staging/controller-manager. Which means the external conversion gen for service controller  v1alpha1 would point to k8s.io/controller-manager instead of kube-controller-manager here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/service/config/v1alpha1/doc.go#L19. Additionally there relevant controllers do depend on a cloud provider implementation. This will be true until cloud provider extraction completes. It does indicate that we will want to deprecate the configuration for service and route from the KCM configuration.
/lgtm
/lgtm

controller code move looks fine. I'm still not sure I understand what it means to move a v1alpha1 config type to the cloud controller module when there is no v1alpha1 top-level version present in that module. This would be a lot clearer to me if it just moved the controller code and kept the config types where they were.

>  I'm still not sure I understand what it means to move a v1alpha1 config type to the cloud controller module when there is no v1alpha1 top-level version present in that module. 

The v1alpha1 types have not moved, they are still in `k8s.io/kube-controller-manager/config/v1alpha1`. This PR only moves the internal config types and the generated code. Do you still prefer that the internal type and generated code stay where they are in `pkg/controller/serivce`?

> Do you still prefer that the internal type and generated code stay where they are in `pkg/controller/serivce`?

I think keeping the config in the module where it is being consumed stays more coherent for now, so yes.
@liggitt updated to leave the config types where they are, sorry for the confusion earlier.

issue_context.title: Move cloud controllers to k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
More cloud providers are adopting/using the out-of-tree cloud providers. One of the various issues / complaints we get is that cmd/cloud-controller-manager is difficult to consume because of the way it pulls in a bunch of other dependencies. 

**Why is this needed**:
I would like to see `cmd/cloud-controller-manager` in staging so it's easier to consume for external providers, however, because it imports controllers in `pkg/controllers/*` it can't be moved there yet. If we also moved the cloud controllers to somewhere like `k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers`, that would unblock us from staging cmd/cloud-controller-manager as well.

I am not sure why we cannot use the same function in node_controller.go and when/where this func will be called?
If this func has to be added here, should the test also be added in node_lifecycle_controller_test.go?
+1, seems like this would be a good start for a controller utils package under cloud-provider.

A little duplication is acceptable here I think. I can't reuse ensureNodeExistsByProviderID from node_controller.go because it is in a separate package and ensureNodeExistsByProviderID is not widely used enough to justify a separate utils package for it either.
